liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let The Good Times Roll** (3 reviews): Opening with this into Franklin's Tower is called a fine way to start the New Year's show; Reviewer found the opening pairing with Franklin's Tower sloppy and uninspired [12][14][22]
- **Drums** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The drums segment with Olatunji is singled out as outstanding; Reviewer's favorite Drums ever, with odd noises they credit to Kitaro [1][12][13]
- **Wang Dang Doodle** (1 review): The show lifts when Clarence Clemons joins the band on this song [14]
- **West LA Fadeaway** (1 review): Clarence Clemons adds power chords on this song, and rocks on every song he plays [19]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): A fairly dark version after a rare late-first-set Cold Rain; Phil is very prominent [14]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The lead-in to The Wheel is called one of the most beautiful ever [18]
- **Gimme Some Lovin'** (1 review): Brent and Phil trade harmonies on this tune after The Wheel emerges from Space [12]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Burns very hot but runs out of gas before the ending [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **Radio Interviews**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [24]
- **Radio Interviews**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [24]
- **Peter Apfelbaum Hieroglyphics Ensemble**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Radio Interviews**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [24]
- **Midnight Madness**: rare: 7 archived performances [24]
- **Radio Interviews**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-12-31.140702.ultramatrix.sbd.pcm.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 247 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd88-12-31.matrix.unknown.3189.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 173 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound quite good, though unchecked against the remaster; Some balloon pops were edited down or removed [2][13]
- **gd1988-12-31.sbd-fm.holtz.lmpp.97786.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 174 min [4]. Said about its sound: Static patches where the receiver drifted off channel, mostly on disc 3, worst during Gimme Some Lovin'; Small left-channel dropouts in Drums were repaired by copying the right channel [4]
- **gd1988-12-31.168751.FM.KFOG.ont.flac1644**: FM broadcast; 24 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Clarence Clemons's saxophone playing is what this show is best remembered for [13]
- Clarence Clemons sounds like a full-time band member throughout the show [16]
- Clarence Clemons plays saxophone with the band at this show [17]
- Playing was looser and more fun-oriented than tight, as at typical New Year's shows [23]
- Clarence Clemons plays sax on part of the show [1]
- Drums features guests Baba Olatunji, Sikiru Adepoju and Kitaro; Clarence Clemons plays sax elsewhere [4]
- Taped on the last night of the New Year's run after missing the ticket lottery [5]
- Reviewer rates it just below the New Year's Eve show of 12/31/81 [17]
- Reviewer thinks Clarence fit the band less well than Branford Marsalis [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-12-31.140702.ultramatrix.sbd.pcm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > PCM Master (Sony F1/Sony PRO-XL500) [1]
- **gd88-12-31.matrix.unknown.3189.sbeok.shnf**: source: Healy Mix (SBD+AKG C 424b mic)> PCM> DAT> DALCardDeluxe> WAV> CD> EAC> SHN [2]
- **gd1988-12-31.sbd-fm.holtz.lmpp.97786.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz; transferred by Brian Green and SIRMick; source: fm > Sony Walkman Fm stereo receiver > Marantz PMD-431 (probably) > mac [4]
- **gd1988-12-31.168751.FM.KFOG.ont.flac1644**: taped by OldNeumanntapr; transferred by OldNeumanntapr; source: KFOG FM Broadcast; Marantz Receiver >Sony WM-D6C [XLIIS / MX 90s] [5]. Also: Recorded from the KFOG FM broadcast in a friend Ron's Oakland living room [5]
